highlights.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
highlights.summary: BBC's Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real.
body: BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real.

Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’” Instead, this time they’re leaving it all in to show a more authentic, organic version of the oceans.

The series features incredible displays of dolphins trapping fish by plugging holes with sea sponges, inter-species fish communication, and 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed. White says that real ocean creatures “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine.”

body: Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund.

Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer.

Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10.
"I knew the start was good. I was gutted at giving him a leg and going into the first break at 4-1 when I wanted 5-0.

highlights.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
highlights.summary: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by…
body: Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad was created. So you might see disclosures pop up in commercials in other states if they’re also expected to air in Pennsylvania.

The law leaves many loopholes, though. For one, what constitutes “significantly modified” is subjective. There is also a carve-out for “parody, satire, commentary or criticism,” as well as anything that is “evidently fictional.” Again, what “evidently fictional” means is unclear. The wording also suggests only content that “uses synthetic content in a manner that creates a false consumer perception” about a product or service would require a disclosure. Again, leaving questions about what qualifies as “false” under the law and who makes those decisions.
The office of State Senator Nick Pisciottano, who introduced the bill, did not immediately return a request for comment.

highlights.title: 5 Cozy Horror Books to Read This Fall That Are Perfect From Start to Finish
highlights.summary: These stories might also lean into childhood nostalgia (think literally any Goosebumps book) or the familiar setting of a small town. Some are lighthearted and comedic; others soften their scares with pleasant elements, dark humor, or wit.
body: Autumn feels cozy and nostalgic, even as the spooky season rolls in. Horror can be an unlikely source of comfort during colder months, and cozy horror books are no exception. Although the definition of “cozy” can be subjective, these books usually balance their frightening elements with low-stakes events and (mostly) happy endings.

Shirley Jackson’s books aren’t traditionally synonymous with cozy horror, but We Have Always Lived in the Castle inspires this sentiment. Even so, the subject matter is grim. Mary Katherine Blackwood lives with her agoraphobic sister Constance and sick uncle Julian inside a huge mansion that is isolated from the village community. The horror lies in the gradual escalation of a “us against the world” mentality, where the characters take refuge in this secluded setting instead of confronting their flaws or seeking help from the world outside. The estate itself feels both eerie and comforting, thanks to the familiar routines that Constance and her sister obsessively follow every day.

highlights.summary: They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham and were described as "awful" by Gary Neville.
body: Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

To add to their woes, on an evening where the dismal weather matched their performance, Cole Palmer was sent off for a second bookable offence after already escaping a straight red card earlier in the game, having barged into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

"Tottenham outplayed Chelsea. Out-coached, everything. None of us expected Tottenham to come here and win today, but after 10-15 mins, that confidence did start to grow," said Neville while on commentary, in a game that was also described as the worst performance of Alonso's short tenure so far.
"Chelsea have been awful, really. On the ball, they've been well short. Nowhere near the level. I am stunned."

highlights.title: Lord of the Rings Officially Returns in November with 3 Releases
highlights.summary: The Lord of the Rings is coming back to physical media in a big way this fall, giving fans another chance to bring a piece of Middle-earth home just as the franchise prepares for its next major chapter.
body: Amazon MGM Studios and Alliance Home Entertainment have announced that the first two seasons of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will receive individual DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K Ultra HD releases in November. The sets will include behind-the-scenes bonus content, while collectors will have another option to consider later in the year.

In December, both seasons will also be released as Amazon-exclusive 4K Ultra HD gift sets featuring Steelbook packaging and collectible art cards. That makes the release particularly timely, with the third season of The Rings of Power set to arrive on Prime Video just days after the standard physical editions hit shelves.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 1 debuted on Prime Video in September 2022, followed by season 2 in August 2024. The series has since become one of the streaming service's biggest shows, with more than 185 million viewers worldwide to date.

Season 3 will pick up with Middle-earth heading deeper into its war against Sauron, with the Dark Lord recruiting men who will eventually become the Nazgûl. He has not yet forged the One Ring, however, leaving the series with plenty of major Tolkien mythology still to explore.

highlights.summary: Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the sitcom “Even Stevens,” has revealed that co-star Shia LaBeouf used to trash-talk competing Disney Channel show “Lizzie McGuire” and that he was “definitely beefing” with the show’s star, Hilary Duff. “Hilary had no clue about that.
body: Last month, ahead of the release of her memoir, “Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star,” Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and water” while guesting on a podcast, despite being just 14 and 12 years old, respectively, at the time.
Romano explained that their on-set incompatibility stemmed from how they were raised.

“I was being raised and brought up to be this type A, I mean exactly like Ren Stevens. Like, you know your lines, you hit your marks, you don’t mess up,” she said. “You’re a New York kid, like that comes with a certain echelon… I was trying to go to pre-college Juilliard… everything we were doing, my mom called it cross-training, came with a certain dollar amount of training.”

In comparison, LaBeouf has long been open about his tumultuous childhood and has said that his father was a recovering addict, and at times abusive. “He was a Venice Beach kind of bum kid,” said Romano. “It’s like that kind of vagrant fun, but also very chaotic and very scary lifestyle, and he was very young to be having that.” She likened his upbringing to the lifestyle depicted in the 1995 Larry Clark film “Kids.”

highlights.title: The moment I knew: I admitted I had a crush on her. She replied, ‘Well, that’s good. Isn’t it?’
highlights.summary: Actors Peter Houghton and Anne Browning played lovers onstage, but a shared sense of humour and a magazine horoscope flipped the script on their real-life relationship. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. Anne and I met in Melbourne in 1997 when we were cast in a production of Hamlet.
body: At first it was a little awkward, but humour was the key. We’d sit on the dusty rehearsal room floor in our tracksuits while the director was working with another actor. Instead of practising our lines, we’d flip through the faded 70s magazines left in the corner and make jokes about what the models in flares or with chopped beards might be saying as they shot the images.

One day by chance I flipped to the horoscopes. I asked Anne what the stars could have in store for us in 1972. She told me her sign was Scorpio – the same as mine. My aim was just to laugh at the bullshit of horoscopes but when I read it out, it stopped me cold: “You have met someone now through work who will be one of the most important people in your life, perhaps a partner and soulmate.”

It was weird and uncanny but we just laughed it off. I felt embarrassed because it sounded like some kind of calculated romantic ploy. I quickly flicked to the next page but somewhere in my brain I knew it was the truth.
points: Actors Peter Houghton and Anne Browning played lovers onstage, but a shared sense of humour and a magazine horoscope flipped the script on their real-life relationship.

LG’s C6 OLED TV offers a few small but welcome upgrades over last year’s C5, including a faster Alpha 11 AI Gen3 processor designed to improve picture and sound quality, along with a brighter display. It also boasts a higher refresh rate of up to 165Hz for smoother gaming, up from 144Hz, while retaining four HDMI 2.1 ports and support for AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, the latter of which helps reduce unwanted screen tearing while gaming.

Unsurprisingly, the C6 delivers the hallmarks of OLED technology, including inky blacks, vibrant color, and impressive contrast. Support for Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, meanwhile, helps make movies and shows appear more lifelike and immersive, while built-in access to Netflix, HBO Max, and the like lets you stream your favorite content without a dedicated streaming device. Google Cast and Apple AirPlay 2 also make it easy to share content from your phone, while Matter support lets you pair it with various smart home devices.

highlights.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
highlights.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

highlights.title: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
highlights.summary: It feels like Apple's Welcome Home event just happened. And the iPhone Duo announcement isn't all that far in our rearview mirror, either. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like.
body: Beyond that? There could be an OLED update for the iPad Mini, plus M6 updates across other devices, following the M6 debut with the Mac Mini in August.

A MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen has been a fixture of the rumor mill since at least early 2023. But now, in late 2026, it may finally come to fruition. The name MacBook Ultra has been floating around, but Apple is unlikely to rebrand its flagship laptop line.

This will be the first touchscreen laptop and the first OLED laptop from Apple. It will supposedly feature an iPhone-esque Dynamic Island, but don’t expect a dramatic revamp of the macOS interface — The touchscreen MacBook isn’t going to be some sort of iPad hybrid. It may include a few flourishes, like a magnification effect when you touch the screen or new gesture controls in native apps. But that’s it.

It’s also going to stick with the M5 series of chips for the time being — specifically, the M5 Pro and M5 Max. There might not be an M6 Pro or Max, even. Instead, Apple may wait to upgrade its higher-end processors until it introduces the M7 next year.

highlights.summary: Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war." The filmmaker behind Skydance-Paramount's upcoming reimagining of Activision's massive first-person shooter series dived into…
body: "And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."

Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job. That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."
"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."

These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.

highlights.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
highlights.summary: Security researchers used AI tools to help uncover years-old vulnerabilities in the PHP web scripting language. Then the AI-assisted attacks began.
body: As security teams and web admins scrambled this week to patch newly public PHP bugs, criminal hackers quickly attempted to exploit the flaws in the wild. Millions of exploitation attempts hit within hours of the vulnerabilities being published, according to analysis from Cloudflare—unsurprising given broad access to AI tools that can make it easier for attackers to quickly exploit flaws.

So far, the nightmare scenario of mass victim takeovers and breaches hasn’t come to pass. The PHP Foundation says it hasn’t seen any successful exploitation of the bugs, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, and many publicly circulating potential exploits appear to be ineffective. However, perhaps the most interesting role of AI amid the chaos this week is how advanced models helped researchers uncover practical exploitations for the vulnerabilities, which were known about, at least in part, for years. In other words, AI helped turn historic vulnerability into a current crisis.
So are we all about to be walloped by a wave of critical vulnerabilities that have been kicking around for decades?

highlights.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
highlights.summary: OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk of affecting…
body: OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September, after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies, or swarm obscure websites. On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says.

Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection.

OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication. It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.”

highlights.title: An AI-Created Design Turned Her Empty Corner into a Breakfast Nook
highlights.summary: “The breakfast nook was one of those spaces that had so much potential but never felt intentional,” Carmen Murphy shares. Carmen and her boyfriend had moved in together two years ago and had been slowly transforming their apartment.But the couple never really did anything with this space — besides…
body: Because Carmen and her boyfriend were renting, she needed to make sure whatever changes she made to the 11-foot-wide space weren’t permanent but still looked built-in. Instead, Carmen turned to ChatGPT “to come up with some options to use the space to its full potential.”
With ChatGPT’s help, Carmen created a layout that fit the small space perfectly and incorporated her three must-haves for the project — more storage, comfortable seating, and her wine fridge.
“I started by measuring the space over and over to make sure every inch would be used efficiently,” Carmen shares. Once she had a plan, she began researching benches that would fit the wall length.

Carmen found that using an L-shaped corner bench and transforming it into a straight built-in bench was the best fit. “It took a lot of measuring and a bit of creative maneuvering to make sure everything lined up, felt balanced, and looked like it had always been there instead of looking pieced together,” she explains.
